title:
If I May But
Touch
paragraphs: Twelve years is long enough to lose count of the doctors, the money, and the hope she started with. By the time this woman reaches Mark chapter five, she isn't looking for a miracle with fanfare — she's done asking permission. She has a crowd between her and Jesus and a law that says her condition makes her untouchable, and exactly one plan left: get close enough to touch the edge of what He's wearing and let faith do what twelve years of doctors couldn't.

Here's the detail that wrecks me every time I read it: dozens of people were touching Jesus that day by accident, pressed against Him in the crush of the crowd, and nothing happened for any of them. Only one touch — hers — carried faith instead of friction. The same power you've been bumping into in church, in scripture, in every ordinary Sunday, is still available the second you stop colliding with God by accident and actually reach for Him on purpose.
